excerpts:

Grok Bot Explained: Email, DMs, and 100+ Weekly Updates
BASENOR Editorial Desk Oct 26, 2026 Updated October 26, 2026 3 min read
Grok Bot Explained: Email, DMs, and 100+ Weekly Updates
Share

Elon Musk took to X on October 26 to ask users what they most want improved in Grok Bot — and in the same breath dropped two pieces of news worth paying attention to.
First, xAI is shipping over 100 features and fixes to Grok every single week. Second, Grok can now reach you directly via email and X DMs, with additional messaging platforms on the way. Here's what you need to know.
Elon Musk tweet asking about Grok Bot improvements and noting 100+ weekly releases Source: @elonmusk — October 26, 2026
What communication channels does Grok Bot support right now?
As of today, Grok Bot can communicate through two channels: email and X Direct Messages. Musk confirmed this in a reply to a user question, making it the first official acknowledgment that Grok has moved beyond the X feed interface into more personal, asynchronous communication formats.
Musk's reply was brief: "Other messaging platforms coming soon." No names, no timeline. Given xAI's integration history with the broader Musk ecosystem — Grok already lives inside Tesla vehicles via voice — the logical candidates include SMS and potentially third-party chat platforms, though nothing has been confirmed.
More than it might seem. Grok Voice 3.0 is already the AI powering in-car conversations in Tesla vehicles, handling millions of interactions daily. Every improvement xAI ships to the underlying Grok model has the potential to flow into the in-car experience — better responses, more accurate answers, smoother conversation handling.

GREG ISENBERG on X: "Grok Bot might be the first tool that lets one non-technical person run an entire business with a team of AI agents.
My friend Billy runs his whole newsletter business on Grok Bot agents, and I think we're about to see 100,000+ businesses like his. BEST PRACTICES: 1. The agents run on a shared cloud computer, so running your newsletter, your X, and your receipts all in one place creates context bloat and burns tokens fast. One mission per setup. 2.
Start with a Chief of Staff. Give it access to your existing docs (Notion, Slack, Gmail), have it audit the business, then tell you the top three agents to build first to drive revenue. 3. Perfect a task with the Chief of Staff before spinning up a new agent.
Have it do the outbound sales once, review it, and only then say "now build a bot that does exactly that." You earn each new hire by proving the task works first. 4. Constraints are the feature. You get a limited number of agents, one thread per bot, like DMs with a teammate.
It forces you to stay mission-oriented instead of spinning up a bot for every random idea. 5. You make the decisions, not the agent. Billy's team spent three weeks unable to pick where content should live. At some point you say "we're doing Notion, no more tinkering" and move on. 6. Run week one with no new agents.
Ask your Chief of Staff what recurring jobs would move the business forward overnight, and it builds the automations that run without you. Thanks to @billyjhowell for sharing the sauce on @startupideaspod (follow for more). Grokbot is really cool. Watch below: youtu.be/qQluNEfSVHk?si…
00:00
